groups.sentence: Users read and understand an AI tool's terms of service and what it does with their content.
Instructors consider copyright and intellectual property when designing course AI policies and discuss them with students.
Users verify that AI output does not infringe copyright, plagiarize or violate third-party intellectual property before using or sharing it.
Users avoid uploading confidential, proprietary, unpublished or others' work to AI tools.
Users read and comply with the terms of use of AI tools and vendors.
Users do not ask AI to reproduce or mimic copyrighted works or claim such output as their own.
Students document AI use in their intellectual property contributions and consider commercialization implications.
The university protects ownership of research and course materials, reviews its guidance regularly and fosters dialogue on AI and IP.
AI output may contain, resemble or reproduce copyrighted material, sometimes without attribution.
Ownership and copyrightability of AI-generated content are unclear, unresolved or limited under current law.
Users do not use AI in ways that infringe copyright or intellectual property rights.
Users comply with copyright and intellectual property laws and respect creators' rights when using AI.
Entering unpublished research or intellectual property into AI tools may count as disclosure and risk losing IP or patent rights.
AI vendors' terms and click-through agreements can bind individuals personally or restrict how AI may be used.
Users seek guidance from relevant offices and policies on AI and copyright.
People keep ownership of their own prompts, work and course materials.
Users clarify who owns AI-generated content and assume it may not be copyright eligible.
Fair use permits some use of copyrighted material, and AI may be used for compliant educational purposes.
